ai.description: The Amboli leaping frog (Ranixalidae) measures 30–40 mm. It is brown with a dark lateral band and bright yellow groin patches. Distinctive features include a pointed snout and long, slender limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Indirana chiravasi* is best identified by the distinct, pale-colored longitudinal stripe running along the center of its back, which is absent in other *Indirana* species.
ai.habitat: *Indirana chiravasi* inhabits the leaf litter of evergreen forests in the northern Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 600 and 900 meters.
ai.behavior: The Amboli leaping frog is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its powerful hind legs to perform long, acrobatic leaps to escape predators or navigate rocky stream beds.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana chiravasi* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 150–200 eggs on wet rock surfaces. It exhibits terrestrial development, bypassing the free-swimming tadpole stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indirana chiravasi* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, specifically found in the Amboli region at elevations between 600 and 800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Amboli Leaping Frog produces a high-pitched, rapid series of "tink-tink" notes, typically heard emanating from rocky, moss-covered stream banks in the Western Ghats.
